definitions.explanation: The dot separating the whole-number part of a figure from its fractional part. Japanese uses the same period as English, and positions after it are counted with {位|くらい} (place).

examples.japanese: {小数点|しょうすうてん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忘|わす}れた→忘れる：00474_wasureru⟧。
{小数点以下|しょうすうてんいか}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{切|き}り{捨|す}てて→切り捨てる：05747_kirisuteru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please drop everything after the decimal point.

examples.japanese: {小数点|しょうすうてん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧⟦{間違|まちが}えた→間違える：01109_machigaeru⟧⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{金額|きんがく}→金額：02665_kingaku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{十倍|じゅうばい}になってしまった。
examples.english: Just one mistake with the decimal point made the amount ten times larger.

notes:
From ⟦{小数|しょうすう}→小数：27356_shousuu⟧ (decimal fraction) plus ⟦{点|てん}→点：01553_ten⟧ (dot). Digits after the point are counted as {小数点|しょうすうてん}{第一位|だいいちい}, {第二位|だいにい}, and so on.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {小数点以下|しょうすうてんいか}: below the decimal point; the fractional part
- {小数点|しょうすうてん}{第二位|だいにい}⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧: to two decimal places
- {小数点|しょうすうてん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧: to put in a decimal point
- {小数点|しょうすうてん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦ずらす→ずらす：20836_zurasu⟧: to shift the decimal point

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{整数|せいすう}→整数：04328_seisuu⟧: whole number, integer — what sits to the left of the point
- ⟦{分数|ぶんすう}→分数：06952_bunsuu⟧: fraction — the other way of writing a non-whole number, with a numerator and denominator
